key_insight: Optimizing curved rectangular vortex generators increased the Colburn heat-transfer factor by 53.1%, while separate pressure-drop-aware optimizations improved area and volume goodness factors by 14.4% and 26.5%, respectively.
engineering_relevance: Tailored vortex-generator geometry can improve water-to-air finned-tube heat exchanger performance while balancing heat-transfer gains against pressure-drop penalties.
method: Used a validated conjugate numerical model of a representative heat exchanger section.
Applied central composite experimental design and nonlinear polynomial regression to four geometry variables: attack angle, curvature angle, axial position and height.
Used a genetic algorithm to optimize heat-transfer-only and pressure-drop-aware objectives.
evidence_signal: Performance gains were evaluated numerically against a reference heat exchanger with plain fins, with different optimized geometries yielding the reported improvements.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish whether the optimized geometries retain their benefits across operating conditions or in full-scale experimental tests.
paper_title: Optimization of curved vortex generator geometry for enhanced thermal performance in water-to-air finned-tube heat exchanger
